item.title: 3 takeaways as Victor Wembanyama's double-double leads Spurs to seventh straight win
item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) defends Sacramento Kings forward Domantas Sabonis (11) during the first half of an NBA basketball game on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. (AP Photo/Jose Luis Villegas) (Jose Luis Villegas/Associated Press) SACRAMENTO, Calif. - Victor Wembanyama cooled off a bit, but it didn't stop him from leading his team to yet another win. Wembanyama finished with 30 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks, Stephon Castle had 19 points and a team-high seven assists, and the Spurs crushed the Sacramento Kings 124-109 Friday night for their seventh straight win in the opening game of NBA Cup group play for both teams. The Spurs' winning streak is the longest in the league this season. Wembanyama's modest - by his standards - stat line came after his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block masterpiece in a 112-111 victory over Dallas on Wednesday night at the Frost Bank Center. "I expect Victor to play the right way," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said when asked if there was a minimum amount of points he expects his star player to produce each game. "He obviously has a tremendous amount of gravity in terms of putting the defense in a tough spot when he's putting pressure on the rim and running the floor and rolling after screens. And I think that's going to produce points, but there are teams that have made very concerned efforts at times of taking that away. And what that should do then is open up opportunities for his teammates." That happened against the Kings in the form of Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell scoring 19 points each on a night the Spurs hit 15 of 30 shots from 3-point range. "We've got a team well-built," Wembanyama said. Said Harper, "We're at our best when everyone's touching the ball, everyone's getting to the paint, kicking out, just making the right play. And it's just a byproduct of our chemistry and how much we generally enjoy playing with each other." Playing on the first night of a back-to-back that ends in Portland and the first outing of a four-game road trip, the Spurs (7-2) took a 19-point lead into halftime Friday after Wembanyama scored 20 points and eight rebounds. Playing 26 minutes overall, he finished 10 of 18 from the field and 4 of 6 from beyond the arc. With his fourth 30-point game of the season and seventh double-double, Wembanyama joined Shaquille O'Neal (1993-94) and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (1975-76) as the only players to post 250 points, 100 rebounds and 35 blocks in the first nine games of a season since blocks became official (1973-74). Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 22 points on an inefficient 9-of-20 from the field to lead the Kings, who fell to 1-8 with their second loss in a row. Domantas Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and five assists for Sacramento. The start of the game was delayed for about 20 minutes due to a mechanical issue with the basket the Spurs shot at during warm-ups. item.title: ‘Some legends don't say goodbye’: Ex-India cricketer's heartfelt message for Mohammed Shami after Test retirement
item.description: Former India cricketer and ex-Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary paid an emotional tribute to Mohammed Shami after the veteran fast bowler announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 12-year career in the longest format. Tiwary, who had the opportunity to lead Bengal with Shami in his bowling attack, took to X to reflect on the pacer's impact and recall his association with the speedster. He described Shami as a warrior, while also highlighting the lasting memories he had created through his performances in the red-ball format. "The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history," Tiwary wrote. — tiwarymanoj (@tiwarymanoj) Recalling his time as Bengal captain, he added: "This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart" Shami's announcement brings an end to an impressive Test career spanning 64 matches, during which he picked up 229 wickets. The 36-year-old made the announcement through an Instagram post, confirming that while he would no longer represent India in the white jersey, he intended to continue playing white-ball cricket. "I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote. "Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added. A 12-year journey in India's Test colours Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. His ability to extract movement through seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a crucial member of India's pace attack across different conditions. Of his 229 wickets, 131 came in 35 Tests played in South Africa, the West Indies and India, where he maintained an average of under 25. South Africa witnessed some of Shami's finest performances in Test cricket. During India's 2018 tour, he produced a match-winning spell of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test, helping the visitors secure a consolation victory. On India's subsequent visit to the country, he continued his impressive record by claiming eight wickets in the series-opening Test at Centurion. Shami's final appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's. Injuries later disrupted his career, and he remained out of the Indian team after the 2025 Champions Trophy, before deciding to bring his red-ball journey to a close.

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives two match points to end Taylor Fritz's ATP Finals hopes
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz survived two match points against Taylor Fritz to book a spot in the last four of the Paris Masters and end his opponent’s hopes of reaching the ATP Finals. In a lengthy contest that lasted two hours and 43 minutes, the second seed lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3. Had Fritz taken one of his opportunities in the second set, he would have locked down the eighth and last place in the end-of-year championship. Instead, that spot now goes to Alcaraz’s fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar. After being outlasted by Fritz in the opener, Alcaraz had to save match points with and against serve in the second, before levelling the scores with three games in a row. He belatedly took control as he closed out the decider in clinical fashion. Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges await the Spaniard in the semi-finals. “I tried not to let myself down in the difficult moments in the second set,” Alcaraz said. Carlos Alcaraz is into the semi-finals of the Paris Masters (Getty) “I tried to stay strong mentally and save those break points and match points. I used the people and the energy and gave them what they really wanted to watch. “I am really happy to play for one and a half hours more to entertain them. The feeling I have today is unmatched.”

item.title: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report
item.description: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that have affected the team this season. According to SPORT , sporting director Deco is examining several possibilities, although the club’s limited financial flexibility in January means finding an affordable reinforcement will be a significant challenge. Barcelona decided against recruiting a central defender during the summer, directing their resources towards strengthening midfield and attack instead. However, an accumulation of defensive injuries exposed the squad’s lack of depth, increasing the urgency to reinforce the position before the second half of the season. Given Barcelona’s financial condition, Deco is exploring loans, affordable transfers and opportunities involving players whose contractual situations could make them accessible. Fikayo Tomori and Vitor Reis among Barcelona’s defensive options On that note, AC Milan’s Fikayo Tomori is one of the leading names under consideration. The English defender’s contract expires in 2027, and Milan are reportedly open to negotiating his departure in January. Interest from several Premier League clubs could nevertheless create competition for his signature. Barcelona are keeping tabs on Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images) Manchester City’s Vitor Reis is another possibility . The Brazilian has struggled for regular opportunities, accumulating just 199 minutes across four appearances this season. A temporary move could offer him valuable playing time, although there is no indication that City are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the season. Piero Hincapie also attracts Barcelona’s attention because of his versatility. The Ecuadorian can operate at both centre-back and left-back, making him particularly suitable for Flick’s defensive requirements. In fact, Deco has already sounded out his representatives about a potential loan with an option to buy. Lisandro Martinez and Lucas Beraldo offer different possibilities Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez is considered another attractive option . His contract situation, experience and ability on the ball make him an interesting candidate, although negotiating with United would not necessarily be easy. item.title: New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final
item.description: Stacey Waaka has represented New Zealand in rugby sevens, rugby union and rugby league [Getty Images] New Zealand (8) 32 Tries: Wiki, Waaka 3, Hufanga, Atai, McGregor Goals: Kiria-Ratu 2 Samoa (0) 0 New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final. It will be the Kiwi Ferns' seventh successive appearance in the showpiece match, but having won the first three between 2000-2008, three trips to the final since then have all ended in heartache. Three consecutive losses to Australia included a blowout 54-4 scoreline four years ago at Old Trafford and unless debutants Fiji spring one of the greatest upsets in the tournament's history in the other semi-final, the Jillaroos are likely to again provide the substantial obstacle to New Zealand becoming four-time champions. However, on Saturday, New Zealand made light of the blustery and difficult conditions inside Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, to make their case as potential winners. Mackenzie Wiki's try - less than two minutes into proceedings, off the back of a Samoa error - set the tone for the Kiwi Ferns. As the storm clouds began to gather overhead, New Zealand's dual-code international Stacey Waaka capitalised on some indecision from Samoa winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala to collect and ground Raecene McGregor's kick. It was efficient and highly professional from New Zealand, who conceded just 24 points across their three group games and once again exhibited their defensive parsimony during a hard-fought first period. A combination of that and Samoa's inability to make the most of field position, with a smattering of handling errors thrown in as well, laid the platform for New Zealand's triumph. There were notable bright spots for the Samoa fans to enjoy. Fanua Rimoni was a powerful and dominant presence at lock forward, while teenage winger Anastasia Leatupue produced a nerveless showing on her international bow. Samoa's biggest disappointment was that they could not get the ball into the hands of the 18-year-old in good attacking positions - with Pauline Piliae-Rasabale twice pulled up for forward passes on the right edge in an error-strewn display. But just like in the first 35 minutes, they had no answer to New Zealand's more potent attacking threat. Waaka was again the beneficiary of a pinpoint McGregor kick as she crossed for her second try and Mele Hufanga held off the attentions of three Samoa defenders tfor her score. It was a feat that was matched by Kaiyah Atai just over two minutes later as New Zealand went through the gears. With Samoa's resistance gradually waning, Waaka capped a fine individual display with her hat-trick and McGregor scored the try her performance richly deserved to round off a fine New Zealand display. item.title: 24 ‘pointless races’ in 10 years: Formula 1 has an end-of-season problem
item.description: Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP’s final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year’s Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi . Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective. Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton ’s all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit. Verstappen lost out in last year's title showdown with Lando Norris (Getty) But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers’ title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport’s ultimate prize on the line. There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory. This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness. Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the “battle for second” or the “best of the rest” tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that. Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten. item.title: Islam Makhachev Drops Major Hint About Retirement, Could Follow Khabib Nurmagomedov’s Lead
item.description: Islam Makhachev’s future in the UFC has been a major talking point over the past few days. The reigning welterweight champion drew plenty of criticism from fans and pundits after reportedly pulling out of negotiations for a fight at UFC 336 . Makhachev was initially expected to defend his 170-pound title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card. However, those plans fell apart after the Dagestani stepped away from the proposed matchup. The champion later explained that the welterweight division had several deserving contenders and believed Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate inside the Octagon. However, the fight negotiations aren’t the only reason Makhachev’s future has come under scrutiny. The two-division champion recently turned 35 on October 27 and has openly discussed the possibility of retirement. He has suggested that he doesn’t have many fights left and wants to spend the remainder of his career facing the toughest available competition. Now, he has offered another hint that his retirement might be closer than expected. Islam Makhachev Says He Will Listen to His Mother When It Comes to UFC Retirement During a recent interview with Red Corner MMA in Tashkent, Makhachev suggested that his career could come to an end much like that of Khabib Nurmagomedov. Interestingly, their mothers could have a say in both decisions. For those unfamiliar, ‘The Eagle’ retired at 32 after promising his mother that he wouldn’t fight again without his father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Following Abdulmanap’s passing ahead of UFC 254, ‘The Eagle’ decided to honor that promise . The Dagestani went on to secure his 29th professional victory against Justin Gaethje in Abu Dhabi before announcing his retirement inside the Octagon. Makhachev now appears to be considering a similar path. He said, “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” The former lightweight champion also admitted that he doesn’t have a specific number of fights in mind before calling it a day. However, he made it clear that he feels his career is nearing its end. item.description: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star Manchester United have not started the 2026/2027 season in any way, shape or form as they would have imagined in August. Season The Red Devils currently sit 17th in the league and have only won one match out of nine. What’s more, they have been dumped out of the League Cup and have won two and lost two of their Champions League matches so far. United signed Senne Lammens last season from Royal Antwerp and he hugely impressed in the United goal, marking a big step up from Andre Onana or Altay Bayindir. Nonetheless, this season has been more of a challenge and even though he has not made many big errors, he has conceded too many goals for a United keeper. Marco Carnesecchi links Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb have jumped on this possible dissatisfaction with the job Lammens is currently doing and linked the club to Atalanta’s Marco Carnesecchi. item.title: ☀️ ADL-Allegri talks, Bastoni insight and Pavlovic doubt: morning news
item.description: ☀️ ADL-Allegri talks, Bastoni insight and Pavlovic doubt: morning news Saturday's action gets underway as Serie A matchday 11 continues (after Udinese's defeat, which also saw Zaniolo lose his cool ), while abroad, negotiations over youngster JJ Gabriel continue to make headlines. Here is this morning's biggest news from Serie A's top clubs. Juventus: Carnevali and his lucky scarf According to Tuttosport , Giovanni Carnevali held up a Juventus scarf during the closing minutes of the Bianconeri's match , which the CEO followed with great emotion. The scarf was a gift from the Board of Directors after a shareholder at the general meeting urged him to pay attention to the symbolic aspects of his new role as well. Carnevali was particularly pleased with the gift and is now expected to carry the scarf with him as a good-luck charm. Milan: Pavlovic doubtful for Genoa According to Corriere dello Sport , Pavlovic did not train with the rest of the squad, instead following an individual programme because of the shoulder discomfort that had already forced him to miss the Europa League clash with Ferencvaros. The Serbian defender therefore remains doubtful for the trip to Genoa : he could play through the pain given the importance of the match, but the final training session will determine whether he can be included in the squad. Inter: The inside story on Bastoni and Barcelona According to The Athletic , Barcelona considered signing Alessandro Bastoni in the summer, with sporting director Deco keen on the move, although Flick had some reservations. In the end, the Catalan club chose to focus on their attack: the coaching staff felt it was essential to sign forwards who could also contribute defensively by pressing high up the pitch. Hence their interest in Anthony Gordon. Barcelona would also reportedly be willing to sell Alejandro Balde as early as January : his contract enters its final year next summer, and there are no reports of renewal talks. A major sale would allow the Blaugrana to fund potential signings in the winter transfer window. Napoli: De Laurentiis reassures Allegri and the squad According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , De Laurentiis visited Castel Volturno, where he spent around three hours discussing Napoli's poor run of results with Allegri and Manna. The president sought to reassure the players before training: "You're good players and good lads too." item.description: Cardiff Devils wore a one-off bespoke uniform, with the game against Dundee Stars designated 'country night'. item.description: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts scores a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have been among the teams interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment suggests a blockbuster deal is unlikely, even with the NFL trade deadline approaching. Green Bay’s rushing offense has struggled through eight games, yet one Packers beat writer believes the reasons go beyond who is carrying the football. And the Packers’ draft-pick situation presents another obstacle. Packers Get Discouraging Jonathan Taylor Trade Assessment The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman cast doubt on Green Bay acquiring Taylor or two other running backs mentioned as trade candidates. “I don’t see the Packers trading for a Jonathan Taylor, Breece Hall or Tony Pollard,” Schneidman wrote. The biggest issue isn’t necessarily Taylor’s talent. Schneidman argued that “the run game’s biggest problem is the blocking,” making an expensive backfield addition a questionable fix. Taylor, a former Wisconsin star and three-time Pro Bowler, might also cost a first-round pick. Green Bay already sent its 2027 first-round selection to Dallas as part of the Micah Parsons trade last year. Even if the Colts lower their demands, Schneidman questioned whether the Packers would part with two middle-round selections. He also didn’t see an obvious Green Bay player who would entice another team in a trade package. Then there’s Josh Jacobs. The veteran returned in October after spending six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and remains under an NFL investigation involving additional allegations. Jacobs said Wednesday that he isn’t concerned about missing more games. Schneidman acknowledged a longer absence for Jacobs could change the Packers’ thinking. Otherwise, acquiring Taylor would create another question: Would Green Bay keep both backs, or try to move Jacobs? He also expressed doubts about the logic of pursuing Pollard, who is at a similar career stage to Jacobs. Taylor and Hall could represent longer-term options, but fitting either alongside Jacobs would be difficult. NFL insider Jordan Schultz also previously named Green Bay among interested teams, along with Minnesota, Denver, Cincinnati and the New York Giants . item.title: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid
item.description: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid Real Madrid are set to take on Valencia at Mestalla later today as they look to continue their excellent form ahead of the international break. The last seven games have been a breeze for Los Blancos , with Jose Mourinho’s side putting in excellent performances. This has been crucial in strengthening belief in the project that the Portuguese manager is building at the Santiago Bernabeu . Mourinho’s men will be looking to make it eight in a row before the November international break. Standing in their way is Javier Aguirre, an experienced manager who has taken over in an attempt to save Valencia’s sinking ship. Aguirre’s struggles against Real Madrid According to Diario AS , the Mexican manager has faced Los Blancos 27 times in his career, securing just four victories. He has suffered 16 defeats and managed seven draws, giving him a win percentage of just 14.8%. Javier Aguirre has a lot of experience managing on the touchline. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) Interestingly, two of his four victories came during his time as Osasuna manager. The first came in February 2003, when he secured a 1-0 victory over Madrid. Vicente del Bosque was Los Blancos ‘ manager at the time. Aguirre followed that up with a 3-0 victory over Madrid in April 2004. His third triumph came in April 2011, when Real Zaragoza secured a stunning 3-2 victory over Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid at the Bernabeu . His most recent victory came in 2023, when Mallorca defeated Carlo Ancelotti’s side 1-0. Can Aguirre trouble Mourinho again? Aguirre is an experienced manager who knows every trick in the book, and he can make life very uncomfortable for Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid. The Mexican is already said to be preparing with a back five ahead of the game in an attempt to stop Los Blancos ‘ attack. Mourinho will hope to make it eight defeats in a row against Valencia. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre has got the better of Mourinho on occasion, but the two sides could hardly be in more contrasting positions heading into this encounter. Real Madrid are the most in-form team in Europe, while Valencia sit 19th, battling relegation and desperately hoping for a turnaround. Los Blancos are playing their fourth consecutive away match and will hope to emerge victorious against Los Che . It promises to be an exciting battle between two experienced managers, and it remains to be seen whether Mourinho can add another defeat to Aguirre’s poor record tonight.

item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images | Getty Images Barcelona look to go into the final international break of the season with a statement win in the bag as the La Liga leaders travel to the capital for a monster top of the table clash against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano . item.title: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms
item.description: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms The link between local music and Manchester City fans has always been present, most obviously through Britpop legends Oasis, and now a new kit release has brought a different Greater Manchester artist to the doorstep. Stockport indie outfit Blossoms, who are also lifelong supporters of the club, have teamed up with the Blues to release a limited run of charity shirts celebrating four decades of local outreach across the region. With City in the Community celebrating its 40th anniversary during the ongoing 2026/27 season, main club sponsor Etihad Airways has stepped aside from their front-of-shirt position to make way for the band's logo on the hugely popular 2024/25 away kit. As announced on the club’s official website this week, the special charity drop puts a new spin on a modern favourite. While Blossoms take over the main shirt sponsor space across the chest, the Etihad Airways logo shifts onto the sleeve, sitting alongside a dedicated CITC logo printed inside the neck to mark the anniversary. Blossoms celebrated their fifth Official UK Number One album with 'Songs From The Wedding Cake' last month and are about to head out on a major arena tour across the country. Anyone hoping to pick up a shirt will have to act fast, with initial sizes dropping exclusively at the new flagship CityStore before further batches go on sale around their upcoming homecoming shows at Manchester's Co-op Live in November and December. Four decades of supporting Greater Manchester Founded back in 1986, City in the Community has spent 40 years delivering health, education, and social inclusion initiatives to youth across Greater Manchester, and all profits from the special shirt drop will go straight to the charity to help sustain its daily programmes and expand its reach throughout the local area. To make an even bigger impact across the campaign, Manchester City will match every fan donation made to the foundation on a pound-for-pound basis until the end of May, up to a total of £200,000. As Enzo Maresca's side keep pushing for results on the pitch, this joint effort between local musicians, sponsors, and Manchester City gives fans another brilliant reason to get behind the community off it. On the pitch, Enzo Maresca and his players will be wanting to maintain the winning performance they showed in the UEFA Champions League and a 2-3 victory at RB Leipzig , and taking those levels into their next Premier League clash away to Nottingham Forest .

item.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
item.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”
